definitions: To suggest or hint (something bad or reprehensible) in an indirect and unpleasant way.
To manoeuvre oneself into a position of favour or office by subtle manipulation.
To introduce (an idea or feeling) into someone's mind in a subtle and indirect way.
examples: He insinuated that she was lying.
She insinuated herself into the director's favour.
The propaganda insinuated doubt into the public's mind.
